title: Specialist-Generalist Fusion with Outcome-Supervised Rationales for Deepfake Detection
V2_relation: 直接强相关；三位CV专家评分及50样本遮挡对照提供有限因果接地证据；无适当依赖/充分性评测
original_reading_scope: arXiv v2官方全文 §§3.3/4.2–4.3、Appendices D/F。
limitations: Three computer-vision experts provide direct artifact-existence judgments; the user study is small (20 descriptions per expert, 60 rating events), and the paper reports no inter-rater reliability or detailed expertise profile. The same 20 stimulus descriptions may be reused across raters; resampling responses does not establish generalization to new images or annotators. The study explicitly selects correctly classified cases, so it does not assess explanation reliability when the detector is wrong, nor appropriate user reliance. The Gemini 7.5% overlap rule and 95.7% claim-support estimate are model-judged, not independent human fact checking; a rationale can contain at least one supported artifact and still omit or misstate others. The cited-region masking test is direct causal evidence of local decision relevance, but covers only 50 correctly classified examples, uses an occlusion intervention that can itself perturb image statistics, and does not test sufficiency/restoration or behavior on errors. Binary-label reward can improve detection without requiring faithful reasoning; authors' output-order control explicitly allows hallucinated explanations. No parameter-randomization, insertion test, or human decision-reliance experiment is reported.
reassessment: 原rank4候选已完成附录全文核读。保留直接强相关；人类评分聚焦伪迹存在，且50例引用区/匹配区遮挡对照支持局部决策相关性；仍需保留小样本、仅正确预测、遮挡副作用、缺充分性/适当依赖等边界。Gemini claim判断需与人评严格分开。

The participant sample was demographically imbalanced (predominantly young, male, technically educated); the study was an online questionnaire; it used only FaceForensics++ and Grad-CAM++; and the authors note its 60-image, uniformly distributed-score, 50%-AI-error design may not match real-world detector performance. reassessment: Keep high priority as human-factors/reliance evidence. Interpret CWS and self-report separately: the heatmap group's CWS advantage over score-only is borderline after Holm correction (p=.048), while raw-accuracy and correct-override pairwise contrasts are nonsignificant; self-reported detector reliance is higher with heatmaps (p=.0499). V2_relation: High-value visual-XAI reliability neighbor: demonstrates explanation-map manipulation in image segmentation under constrained output/input changes.

Experiments include an industrial peach dataset, an aerial-drone dataset, and COCO; the dissertation also surveys image-segmentation XAI and notes forensic segmentation examples are limited to iris work.
limitations: Strong explanation-robustness method neighbor, not an image-forgery/authenticity experiment. It evaluates attack susceptibility and map similarity rather than explanation truth for natural forensic edits. Forensic examples in its survey concern post-mortem iris segmentation, not tampering detection.
reassessment: Strong visual explanation-robustness method evidence; no direct image-forensics task.

title: Do feature attribution methods correctly attribute features?
V2_relation: Strong general visual-XAI correctness method neighbor: controlled image artifacts provide known decision-relevant regions for attribution tests.
original_reading_scope: Image classification with deliberately introduced data-collection artifacts. The study creates known effective regions by pairing label reassignment with blur, brightness, hue, pixel-noise, and watermark manipulations, then tests Gradient, SmoothGrad, GradCAM, LIME, and SHAP on ResNet34.
limitations: Image-domain controlled classification study, not image forgery/authenticity detection. Its intervention-derived regions are useful as known-effect controls, but do not automatically equal natural manipulation evidence. Merge the workshop and arXiv versions into the AAAI 2022 work identity.
reassessment: High-value image-domain validity evidence; no direct forensic task.

title: Recovering localized adversarial attacks
V2_relation: Strong image-domain controlled-ground-truth method neighbor: compares saliency maps with known localized perturbation regions.
original_reading_scope: Constructs localized iterative adversarial attacks on 112 images, yielding 608 successful attack examples; compares salience, guided backpropagation, and LIME maps against the known attack region using Jaccard/overlap measures.
limitations: General image classification, not image forensics. The manipulated mask is a causal proxy for a designed attack, not necessarily a complete or unique explanation of either class because the model may rely on pixels outside the attacked area too.
reassessment: Useful region-recovery benchmark design; external validity to natural image manipulation remains untested.

Ten institutionally recruited adults and a geographically concentrated annotation pool limit generalization. OOD grounding drops more than text similarity in the paper's narrative, but the extracted PDF table has font-encoding issues, so no uncertain table values are transcribed here. The paper is arXiv v1; only that version was reviewed. All 70 references received title/topic screening, not 70 cited-work full-text reviews.

original_reading_scope: Visually reviewed the 16-page official SSRN PDF: body pages 1-14 (abstract/introduction, related work, framework/objective, data split, results/figures, conclusion and declarations). limitations: Eq. (2)/algorithm and Figure 2 are inconsistent about whether the training alignment loss takes an absolute difference; absent verified code, the trained objective cannot be confidently characterized as pixelwise MAE.
